dlg_006: ☁️ How to get a Google Cloud TTS API key
dlg_007: 1. Sign In & Enable API: • Go to cloud.google.com/text-to-speech (button below), sign in with your Google account, and click the blue button in the center. • Type text to speech in the top search bar, select Cloud Text-to-Speech API, and click Enable. 2. Billing Account (required for the free tier): • Google will ask to enable billing: click Enable billing → Create billing account (create a project too if needed). • In the form, select Account type: Individual (not Organization), Tax info: Personal, and enter your name, address, and postal code. • Link a bank card — it must have at least ~ (or ~10 UAH) for temporary verification. Sometimes Google's billing form behaves oddly and asks to enable billing or re-enter details a second time — that's normal, just click Enable and confirm again. 3. Create an API Key: • Open Credentials (key icon) in the left menu and click + Create Credentials → API key at the top. • Give it a name, select Cloud Text-to-Speech API under Select API below, scroll down, and click Create. • Copy the key and paste it into the API key field in this app (it saves automatically). 🛡️ The app has built-in quota protection so your card will never be charged by accident. To unlock paid models, click 💳 Switch to Paid in the Google Cloud TTS section.
dlg_009: 🎙️ How to get an ElevenLabs API key
dlg_010: 1. Sign Up & Create Key: • Go to elevenlabs.io, sign up or sign in, and open API Keys (button below). • Click Create Key and enter any name. • Important: enable these permissions for the key: — Text-to-Speech → Access — Voices → Read — Voice Collections → Read • Click Create Key at the bottom right, copy the key, and paste it into the API key field in this app (it saves automatically). 2. Plans, Credits & Models: • Click your profile avatar → Upgrade to check your remaining quota or pick a paid plan. • There is no separate «switch to paid» button here — the app gives direct access to Flash, Turbo, and Multilingual models. Flash is recommended for everyday speech (fastest and uses fewer credits), while Multilingual delivers top quality. 3. Using a Voice from the Website (Voice ID): • In the left menu on the site, open Text to Speech or Voices, pick a language and voice you like (voices with a lock icon may require a paid plan). • Click the three dots ... next to the voice → Copy Voice ID and paste it into the Voice ID field in this app (or click 🔄 Refresh voices to load voices from your account).
dlg_012: 🤖 How to get an OpenAI TTS API key
dlg_013: 1. Sign Up & Create Key: • Go to platform.openai.com and sign in or create an account. • In the left menu open API keys (or click the button below), then click + Create new secret key at the top right. • Enter any name, create the key (starts with sk-...), copy it, and paste it into the API key field in this app (it saves automatically). 2. Billing & Balance (important!): • OpenAI API has no free tier or monthly subscriptions (even if you have ChatGPT Plus, API billing is separate). • It is strictly pay-as-you-go: open Billing (click Go to billing), add a payment card, and top up your balance (usually from ) — TTS will not work without credits. 3. Choosing a Model in the App: • Select your preferred model in the OpenAI section: tts-1 (fast and cheapest), tts-1-hd (higher audio quality), or gpt-4o-mini-tts (newest model with natural intonation).
dlg_015: 🐟 How to get a Fish Audio API key and voice ID
dlg_016: 1. Sign Up & API Key: • Go to fish.audio and click Sign Up (signing in with a Google account is the fastest way). • Open API Keys (button below), click the black Create API Key button at the top right, enter any name, and click Create. • Copy the key and paste it into the API key field in this app (it saves automatically). 2. Credits & Paid Mode: • You get 8,000 free credits renewed monthly. Click your avatar at the top right to view your remaining credits and renewal date, or click Upgrade to subscribe (e.g. 250,000 credits/month). • If you have a paid plan and want to use paid models, click 💳 Switch to Paid in the app (below the Guide button). 3. Adding a Catalog Voice or Cloning Your Own: • Open Text-to-Speech on the website, add a voice you like, then click Copy Model ID on the right. You can also clone your own voice on the site by uploading a short audio sample and copy its ID the same way. • Paste that ID into the Voice ID field in the app (or click 🔄 Refresh voices). • Important: to make the voice appear in the list, select its matching language in the dropdown on the right (for example, select Russian for a Russian voice, otherwise it won't show up).
dlg_018: ✨ How to get a Google AI Studio (Gemini TTS) API key
dlg_019: 1. Sign in to Google AI Studio: • Go to aistudio.google.com, click Get started, and sign in with your Google account. • Click the key icon at the bottom left (or open the page via the button below). 2. Create a Project (required if you don't have one): • In the left menu open Projects, click Create a new project at the top right, enter any name, and click Create. 3. Create an API Key: • Go back to API keys in the left panel and click Create API key at the top right. • Enter a name, select your newly created project from the bottom dropdown list, and click Create key. • Copy the key (starts with AIza...), paste it into the API key field in this app (saves automatically), and pick a model from the list (default is gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts, works on the free tier).

ui_086:
Hey! Meet SilentVoice — your text-powered voice
Can't or don't feel like talking into a mic? Just type, and the app will speak for you — in calls, games, or on stream. It's a huge help both for people who can't speak vocally and for anyone who prefers communicating by typing.

Set up in a minute:
1. Pick a speech engine. Head to "🎙️ Voice & Speech" and install any TTS engine: offline under "📦 Download to PC" or online under "☁️ Online Voices" (free Edge-TTS is the easiest place to start).
2. Choose a voice. At the top under "Your active voice", pick a voice you like and give it a quick test.
3. Use it anywhere. Press {hk_toggle} over any app or game, type your message, and hit {hk_send} — others will hear you right away!

💡 Tip: to send your voice into Discord or games, enable VB-Cable in the "🔊 Audio & System" tab.

ui_196: Why have a Primary and Fallback TTS?
ui_197:
Two-layer voice reliability:

• Primary TTS — your main everyday voice.
• Fallback TTS — takes over automatically if the primary voice fails (internet drops, API error, or quota limit).

💡 Tip: If your primary voice is online (Edge-TTS, ElevenLabs, OpenAI, etc.), install one local voice (e.g. Silero or Piper) as your Fallback TTS so you never lose your voice.

Each selected TTS gets its own independent sound settings below.

ui_204: ✂️ Split text into sentences for speech (at ., ! and ?)
ui_207: Long text is split at sentence endings (., !, ?) and spoken one sentence at a time, without splitting at commas. This starts speech sooner, syncs OBS subtitles, and helps prevent cutoffs.
ui_208: 🔢 Convert numbers & symbols (%, $, °, #) into words for speech
ui_211:
Why use this?
Some voices (especially local ones) struggle with digits or skip symbols like %, $, €, ₴, °C, or №.

• For speech: numbers and symbols are expanded into words so they sound natural.
• On screen, in OBS & history: the original text stays intact (e.g. 50% off).

If your voice already reads numbers cleanly, you can turn this off.
ui_216:
What does it do?
Automatically fixes typos, punctuation, and wrong keyboard layout (e.g. ghbdsn → привіт) before speaking or showing in OBS.

How to set up:
1. Pick a provider (fastest free option is Groq) and click + Add.
2. Paste your API key (see the 📘 Guide button for steps).
3. Check the "AI Spellcheck" box (or click ⚙️ to choose primary/fallback services and prompt).

If you don't need automatic text cleanup, simply leave the checkbox off.

When is it active?
Audio processing turns on automatically as soon as any control below is adjusted.

• Speed — makes speech faster (above 1.00x) or slower (below 1.00x) without changing pitch.
• Pitch (Higher / Lower) — positive (+) sounds lighter and higher; negative (-) sounds deeper.
• Noise reduction — removes metallic artifacts and faint synth hiss.
• De-esser (S / SH softening) — smooths harsh sibilant sounds.
• Studio noise gate — silences background hum in pauses between words.

If your voice already sounds great as-is, you don't need to change anything.

ui_366: How to make other people hear your TTS voice?
ui_367:
How audio routing works:
For others to hear you in Discord, games, or calls, the sound is sent through the virtual VB-Cable.

• Channel 1 (For others): sends the voice as a microphone (CABLE Input). Select CABLE Output as your microphone in Discord or games.
• Channel 2 (For you): plays the sound through your headphones or speakers so you can hear the speech yourself.
ui_369:
In simple terms:
Windows does not let one app “speak” directly into your microphone.

• VB-Cable creates a virtual microphone.
• SilentVoice sends the speech to it, and Discord, Skype, or games see it as your regular microphone.

ui_427: What is SOCKS5 and how to use it?
ui_428:
When do you need this?
Only if OpenAI, Gemini, ElevenLabs, Groq, or Fish Audio are unavailable in your region and you do not want to change the network connection for your entire PC.

• Already using a system-wide network connection? You do not need this option — everything will work automatically.

• Running V2Ray / v2rayN / Hiddify / Nekoray / Clash / Tor in local mode without affecting game ping? Check “Use SOCKS5” and leave the address empty. The app will auto-detect the local port.

• Have a custom SOCKS5 server? Check the box and enter its address (e.g. 127.0.0.1:10808 or user:pass@ip:port).

If online services already work directly, leave this unchecked.

ai.guide.groq.title: ⚡ How to get a Groq API key (free and very fast)
ai.guide.groq.html: 1. Go to console.groq.com/keys and sign in to your account. 2. Click Create API Key, give it any name, and copy the key (starts with gsk_...). 3. Paste the key into the API key field in the Groq API card. 4. Tip: Groq is the fastest (usually 150–300 ms) and offers a generous free tier.

ai.guide.gemini.html: 1. Open aistudio.google.com/apikey and sign in with your Google account. 2. Click Create API key and copy the key (starts with AIza...). 3. Paste the copied key into the API key field in the Google Gemini API card.
ai.guide.openai.title: 🤖 How to get an OpenAI API key
ai.guide.openai.html: 1. Open platform.openai.com/api-keys. 2. Click + Create new secret key and copy the key (sk-...). 3. Paste the key into the API key field in the OpenAI API card.
ai.guide.openrouter.title: 🌐 How to get an OpenRouter API key
ai.guide.openrouter.html: 1. Go to openrouter.ai/keys and sign in. 2. Click Create Key and copy the key (sk-or-...). 3. Paste the key into the API key field in the OpenRouter API card.
ai.guide.deepseek.title: 🐳 How to get a DeepSeek API key
ai.guide.deepseek.html: 1. Go to platform.deepseek.com/api_keys and sign in. 2. Click Create new API key and copy the key (starts with sk-...). 3. Paste the key into the API key field in the DeepSeek API card.

ai.guide.zai.html: 1. Go to z.ai/manage-apikey/apikey-list (or chat.z.ai → API) and sign in. 2. Create a new API key and copy it. 3. Paste the key into the API key field in the Z.ai API (GLM) card.
ai.guide.ollama.title: 🖥️ Ollama: quick guide
ai.guide.ollama.html: 1. If Ollama is not installed, click Install Ollama. 2. To use another model, open the library below. Copy the model name and tag (for example, qwen2.5:3b) from its page and paste it into the model field. 3. Click Download model. Progress appears here. The model is marked as installed only after the download completes successfully. Smaller models usually need less memory. Larger ones may be more capable but slower. The model corrects text; it does not change the speaking voice. If installed, Ollama starts when you enable the AI corrector. Start LM Studio, llama.cpp, and other apps and their servers separately. No commands are needed in SilentVoice.
ai.prov.local_api.title: Other local server
ai.guide.local_api.title: 🖥️ Connect another local model
ai.guide.local_api.html: This works with Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, or another app that provides an OpenAI-compatible API. For Ollama, the Ollama card above is simpler. GGUF, BF16, and similar labels describe model files. A file sitting on your PC cannot be selected here by itself. 1. Open it in an app that supports its format, such as LM Studio or llama.cpp for GGUF. 2. Turn on that app's local server. 3. Copy the server address into this field and click Refresh models. The list shows models the server currently provides. The ⋯ button opens this window to look for a model in another app. The server must support the file format. SilentVoice starts Ollama when the corrector is enabled; start other apps and their servers yourself. You do not need to enter commands in SilentVoice.

tg.guide.title: 🤖 How to connect @silero_voice_bot via Telegram
tg.guide.html: 1. Connecting Your Telegram Account: • In the Silero Bot (Telegram) section click Connect Telegram — the app interacts with the bot through your Telegram account. • Sign in via QR code (Settings → Devices → Link Desktop Device) or phone number. If two-factor authentication (2FA) is enabled, enter your Telegram cloud password. • Advanced users may optionally replace the built-in API keys with their own (my.telegram.org/apps), though it is not required. 2. Limit & Required Channel Subscription: • The free tier limit in the bot is about 666 characters (for regular use you can buy an inexpensive plan inside the bot). • Note: in free mode the bot may ask you to subscribe to its news channel. Click 🔊 Listen test in the app — if a subscription is required, the bot will send the channel link in Telegram. 3. Adding & Selecting Voices: • Click ➕ Add voice: enter a code manually or pick a voice directly in the Telegram bot (Choose voice → filter → open voice → Select) — it will be added and the dialog will close automatically. • If you selected a voice in the bot earlier, click 🔄 From bot (/speaker) to sync the latest active voice.

dlg.local_notice.title: Local Model Preparation
dlg.local_notice.body:
Don't worry if the very first phrase takes a while!

• Why it happens: each time you open the app, this voice needs 10–40 seconds to get ready (most noticeable right after installation).
• After that, it's fast: from the 2nd phrase onward until you close the app, speaking takes only 1–2 seconds.
• You'll rarely feel it later: SilentVoice usually loads the voice quietly in the background right after launch, so you only wait if you speak within the first few seconds.

So if the first phrase takes a bit to generate — hang on and be sure to try a second one.

dlg.qwen_quant.body:
Which Qwen 1.7B quantization would you like to install?

• Qwen 1.7B (Q8) — better voice quality, but higher video memory usage (~3± GB VRAM).
• Qwen 1.7B (Q5) — slightly lower quality, but lower video memory usage (~2.2 GB VRAM).

If you have less than 9 GB of VRAM and want to play games while running the app, Q8 may not leave enough VRAM for your game.

ov.guide.header: 🎭 How to get the best cloned voice in OpenVoice
ov.guide.body:
What it does: OpenVoice shifts any TTS voice toward your chosen file. It alters the voice quite roughly, but barely loads your PC and still adds some individuality.

Where to get a sample:
• Cut a clean voice clip from any video or online recording.
• Or use ElevenLabs, Fish Audio, or similar services (free starter credits): pick a voice, paste the text below, and download the file.

File tips: 10–25s (best ~12–18s), single speaker, no music/noise/echo, steady natural volume.

clone.guide.header: 🎭 How to get the best cloned voice in {engine_title}
clone.guide.body:
What it does: {engine_title} speaks your text directly in the timbre and style of your selected audio sample.

Where to get a voice sample:
• Cut a clean speaking clip from any recording or video online.
• Or sign up on ElevenLabs, Fish Audio, or a similar service (free starter credits included), pick a voice, paste the script below, and download the generated audio file.

Tips for the cleanest result:
• Length: 6–20 seconds (sweet spot ~8–15s).
• Clean audio: single speaker only—no music, game SFX, noise, or echo.
• Delivery: steady natural volume without whispers, shouting, or clipping, with short pauses and varied intonation.

Clean audio when changing speed and pitch:
When FFmpeg is installed, the app adjusts speech speed and pitch using asetrate/atempo without metallic artifacts.

• Click "Install FFmpeg" to automatically download ffmpeg.exe into data/engines/ffmpeg (~114 MB).

input.game_mode_help_body:
Why is this helpful in games?
During blind typing, SilentVoice captures WASD, Space, and letters so your character does not move while typing.

• In combat: if an enemy surprises you, clicking LMB/RMB (shoot/aim) or making a sharp mouse flick instantly cancels typing and returns controls to the game.
• Outside games: in Discord, browsers, or on desktop, protection stays inactive so typing behaves normally.
• Draft: unfinished text can be kept for a set time and restored after the fight.

When not typing, the mouse is not monitored at all — zero impact on FPS, aim, or anti-cheats.

Accidental close protection:
If you haven't finished typing and close the input (Esc, hotkey, or button), your text is kept as a temporary draft.

Reopening typing within the seconds set on the right automatically restores your unfinished text.
